summary: Flags unnecessary 'return;' statements at the end of functions where execution would naturally fall through.
firingShapes: function f() { if (c) { y(); return; } z(); }
function f() { label: break label; return; }
function f() { if (x) return; else return; }
silentShapes: function f() { if (x) { return; } else { throw; } }
fixDescription: Remove the 'return;' statement entirely when it appears as the last statement in a function body and control flow would reach the function end without it.
hazards: Removing 'return;' in a function that is the target of a label break changes control flow if the label is outside the function.
In a function with a finally block, removing a return before the finally may cause the finally block to execute when it previously would not have due to the return skipping it.
If the function is called via eval or indirect call, removing the return could affect the value of 'this' in strict mode if the function relies on implicit return undefined vs explicit return.
In a function that is a getter, removing an explicit return; may be misinterpreted by tools expecting a value, though runtime behavior remains undefined.
If the return statement has a trailing comment, the autofix may drop the comment if not handled properly, altering source formatting.
In async functions, removing a return; is safe because it still returns a resolved promise with undefined, but tools may misinterpret intent.
In generators, removing a return; is safe as it yields done:true with undefined, but may confuse static analysis expecting explicit termination.
If the function is part of a comma-separated expression, removing the return; could change the value produced if the function expression's value is used.
